questions.explanation: A bicycle's front lamp must be visible from 300 feet so drivers and pedestrians can spot it in the dark.

quizzes.title: Bicyclist & Pedestrian Safety Test #2
quizzes.description: Practice California's Daylighting Law, the Freedom to Walk Act, and pedestrian crosswalk rules with 20 DMV-style questions.

questions.question: The Daylighting Law is designed to improve visibility at intersections by restricting what?
options: Streetlight brightness
Vehicle parking near crosswalks
Bicycle traffic
questions.explanation: The law keeps the area near crosswalks clear of parked cars so sightlines between drivers and pedestrians stay open.

questions.question: When did active enforcement of California's Daylighting Law begin?
options: January 1, 2023
January 1, 2024
January 1, 2025
questions.explanation: The law technically took effect January 1, 2024, but enforcement of the parking restriction didn't start until January 1, 2025.

questions.question: Why does the Daylighting Law prohibit parking near crosswalks even where there is no red curb painted?
options: Red curb paint is being phased out statewide
The visibility problem exists whether or not a curb is marked
It only applies to streets without curbs
questions.explanation: The restriction applies regardless of curb markings because a parked car blocks sightlines whether or not it's sitting on painted red curb.

questions.question: Under the Freedom to Walk Act, is it legal for a pedestrian to cross outside of a marked crosswalk in California?
options: No, it is always illegal
Yes, as long as it can be done safely with no immediate danger of a collision
Yes, but only at night
questions.explanation: The law decriminalized safe midblock crossing, so pedestrians can cross outside a crosswalk if doing so doesn't create an immediate hazard.

questions.question: What year did the Freedom to Walk Act take effect in California?
questions.explanation: The Freedom to Walk Act (AB 2147) became law on January 1, 2023.

questions.question: Under the Freedom to Walk Act, a pedestrian can still be cited for crossing outside a crosswalk if:
options: They are wearing headphones
Their crossing creates an immediate danger of a collision
They cross more than once in the same day
questions.explanation: The law only protects safe crossings; a pedestrian who steps into traffic and creates a real collision risk can still be cited.

questions.question: At a marked crosswalk, who generally has the right-of-way?
options: Drivers
Pedestrians
Whoever signals first
questions.explanation: Drivers are required to yield to pedestrians who are crossing within a marked crosswalk.

questions.question: Besides slowing down, what else must a driver do when approaching a pedestrian in a crosswalk?
options: Exercise due care and take whatever action is needed to protect the pedestrian's safety
Only proceed if the pedestrian waves them through
Sound the horn before proceeding
questions.explanation: Drivers have an ongoing duty of care toward crosswalk pedestrians, not just a speed requirement.

questions.question: Even where there is no marked crosswalk, pedestrians have the right-of-way over vehicles at:
options: Any midblock location
Intersections
Freeway on-ramps
questions.explanation: An unmarked crosswalk still legally exists at most intersections, and drivers must yield there just as they would at a painted one.

questions.question: Which e-bike class provides pedal-assist power up to 28 mph?
options: Class 1
Class 2
Class 3
questions.explanation: Class 3 e-bikes are the fastest category, assisting the rider's pedaling up to 28 mph.

questions.question: What distinguishes a Class 2 e-bike from a Class 1 e-bike?
options: Class 2 can be propelled by throttle without pedaling
Class 2 has a higher top assisted speed
Class 2 requires a driver's license
questions.explanation: Both classes top out at 20 mph of assistance, but Class 2 adds throttle-only operation, which Class 1 doesn't have.

questions.question: Does California require registration or a license plate for a legally classified e-bike?
options: Yes, all e-bikes must be registered
No, Class 1-3 e-bikes are not treated as motor vehicles for registration purposes
Only Class 3 e-bikes need registration
questions.explanation: As long as an e-bike has working pedals, stays within the 750-watt limit, and fits one of the three classes, it's exempt from DMV registration, plates, and insurance.

questions.question: Which situation permits a cyclist to ride away from the right-hand edge of the road?
options: Preparing to turn left
Riding below the posted speed limit
Carrying a passenger
questions.explanation: Setting up for a left turn is one of the specific exceptions that lets a cyclist leave the right edge of the roadway.

questions.question: In California, who decides whether cyclists may ride on sidewalks?
options: The DMV, on a statewide basis
Local city or county ordinances
The California Highway Patrol
questions.explanation: There's no single statewide rule on sidewalk cycling; it's left to individual cities and counties to regulate.

questions.question: What is the general rule for a cyclist's lane position when traveling at the same speed as surrounding traffic?
options: They must still hug the right edge of the road
They are not required to ride at the right edge
They must dismount and walk the bike
questions.explanation: The requirement to stay near the right edge only applies to cyclists moving slower than the flow of traffic.

questions.question: What is the minimum passing distance a motorist must give a bicyclist under California law?
options: 2 feet
3 feet
4 feet
questions.explanation: State law sets a three-foot minimum clearance when a vehicle overtakes a cyclist in the same lane.

questions.question: A 2023 amendment to the Three Feet for Safety Act added what additional requirement for drivers passing a cyclist?
options: Reduce speed to 15 mph before passing
Change lanes when feasible before passing
Honk twice before passing
questions.explanation: The amendment requires drivers to move into another lane when it's feasible and safe, rather than squeezing past in the same lane.

questions.question: In California, bicycle helmets are legally required for riders under what age, regardless of e-bike class?
questions.explanation: Anyone under 18 must wear a helmet on any bicycle or e-bike, on top of the extra Class 3 rule that applies to all ages.

questions.question: What color must a bicycle's rear reflector or light be for legal night riding?
options: Red
White
Yellow
questions.explanation: The rear of a bicycle must show a red reflector or red light visible to traffic approaching from behind.

questions.question: Besides a front lamp and rear reflector, what other reflective equipment does California law require for night riding, unless the bike has reflectorized tires?
options: Pedal or ankle reflectors
A rearview mirror
A horn
questions.explanation: Reflectors on the pedals or the rider's ankles help make the bike visible from the front and rear at night.

quizzes.title: Bicyclist & Pedestrian Safety Test #3
quizzes.description: Review California's bicycle equipment, helmet, and passing-distance requirements with 18 DMV-style practice questions.

questions.question: How many classes of e-bikes does California law officially recognize?
questions.explanation: California defines three e-bike classes, Class 1, 2, and 3, each with its own speed and throttle rules.

questions.question: Which e-bike class has no throttle-only mode and stops assisting the rider at 20 mph?
options: Class 1
Class 2
Class 3
questions.explanation: Class 1 e-bikes only assist while pedaling and cut off at 20 mph, unlike Class 2's throttle option or Class 3's higher speed cap.

questions.question: A 15-year-old wants to ride a Class 3 e-bike on a public road in California. Is this permitted?
options: Yes, as long as they wear a helmet
No, the minimum age for Class 3 is 16
Yes, but only with a parent riding alongside
questions.explanation: Class 3 e-bikes have a 28 mph assisted top speed and a statewide minimum operating age of 16, so a 15-year-old cannot legally ride one on the road.

questions.question: Which California law addresses visibility problems caused by vehicles parked too close to crosswalks?
options: Three Feet for Safety Act
Daylighting Law
Freedom to Walk Act
questions.explanation: The Daylighting Law is the one that targets parking too close to a crosswalk or intersection corner.

questions.question: Under the Daylighting Law, is it illegal to park close to a crosswalk even if there's no red curb painted there?
options: Yes
No
Only on weekends
questions.explanation: The parking restriction applies regardless of curb color, so a lack of red paint doesn't make close parking legal.

questions.question: The Three Feet for Safety Act specifically regulates the behavior of:
options: Cyclists passing pedestrians
Drivers passing cyclists
Pedestrians crossing streets
questions.explanation: This law sets the minimum distance a motor vehicle must keep when overtaking a bicyclist.

questions.question: If a full lane change isn't possible when passing a cyclist, what must a driver do instead?
options: Pass at normal speed anyway
Slow to a safe speed and pass only when it won't endanger the cyclist
Stop completely and wait for the cyclist to pull over
questions.explanation: When conditions don't allow a lane change or the full three feet, the driver must slow down and only pass when it's safe to do so.

questions.question: A driver approaching a marked crosswalk with a pedestrian in it must do what?
options: Yield and use due care
Only yield if the pedestrian is running
Proceed if there's no stop sign nearby
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield the right-of-way and exercise due care whenever a pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.

questions.question: Which crosswalk type requires drivers to yield to crossing pedestrians even though it has no painted lines?
options: An unmarked crosswalk at an intersection
A crosswalk inside a parking lot
A crosswalk on a freeway on-ramp
questions.explanation: California law treats most intersections as having an unmarked crosswalk, and drivers must yield there just as at a painted one.

questions.question: Outside of any crosswalk, which rule requires a pedestrian to yield to close vehicles?
questions.explanation: CVC 21954 flips the right-of-way rule for pedestrians crossing outside a crosswalk, requiring them to yield to nearby vehicles.

questions.question: Which age group must wear a helmet while riding any bicycle or e-bike in California?
options: Riders under 18
Riders over 65
All riders regardless of age
questions.explanation: The base helmet law covers all bicyclists and e-bike riders under 18, with an added rule for Class 3 riders of any age.

questions.question: A parent riding an e-bike with a child passenger seat must make sure the child, if under 18, wears what safety equipment?
options: A helmet
Elbow pads only
Nothing is required for passengers
questions.explanation: California's helmet requirement covers passengers under 18 as well as the person operating the bike.

questions.question: What must a bicycle have to be ridden legally after dark in California?
options: A horn and mirror
A front white lamp and a rear red reflector or light
A license plate
questions.explanation: Night riding requires a visible front white light and a rear red reflector or light so the bike can be seen from both directions.

questions.question: From what distance must a bicycle's front lamp be visible at night?
options: 100 feet
300 feet
1,000 feet
questions.explanation: The front lamp must be bright enough to be seen from 300 feet away.

questions.question: Whether cyclists may ride on sidewalks in California is decided by:
options: State law, uniformly statewide
Local city or county ordinances
The DMV, case by case
questions.explanation: There's no single state rule on sidewalk riding, so it varies from one city or county to the next.

questions.question: A cyclist is generally required to ride as far right as practicable, except when:
options: The lane is too narrow to safely share with a car
The cyclist is tired
It is raining
questions.explanation: A substandard-width lane is one of the specific conditions that lets a cyclist move away from the right edge.

questions.question: When passing another cyclist traveling in the same direction, is a rider permitted to briefly move away from the right edge of the road?
options: Yes, passing is a recognized exception to the ride-right rule
No, cyclists may never leave the right edge
Only if they honk first
questions.explanation: Overtaking another rider or vehicle is one of the built-in exceptions to the requirement to stay near the right edge.

questions.question: Since the Freedom to Walk Act took effect, can police cite a pedestrian just for crossing mid-block?
options: Yes, always
No, only if the crossing creates an immediate danger of a collision
Yes, but only in downtown areas
questions.explanation: A safe mid-block crossing is no longer citable on its own; police can only cite it if it actually creates an immediate collision risk.
